title: Film Score
tagline: Music composed to shape a film's emotion, rhythm, and sense of place.
summary: Film scores use orchestral, electronic, and popular-music techniques to support a movie's story and visual world. Composers develop themes, textures, and rhythms that can guide attention or deepen a scene's emotional impact. The form spans silent-era accompaniment through contemporary studio recordings and concert performance.

pillars.name: John Williams
pillars.why: Williams is known for memorable orchestral themes written for major film franchises and standalone films.

pillars.name: Ennio Morricone
pillars.why: Morricone developed a distinctive cinematic sound using orchestral writing, unconventional timbres, and vocal textures.

pillars.name: Bernard Herrmann
pillars.why: Herrmann's scores used bold orchestration and musical motifs that became closely associated with classic cinema.
